paras.en: Or they might not build a good sales and marketing team, or their strategies might not work, or they might run into 'complexities and risks' with enterprise sales. Or they might provide bad customer support. Or the new products might not work out. Or there might be technical failures, including elsewhere such as the cloud services. Or they might not make acquisitions and investments, or they might not integrate them, or the regulatory bodies might not approve those acquisitions. They might not be able to integrate with other software, or get kicked out of the app stores.
paras.zh: 或者他们可能无法组建优秀的销售与市场团队，或其策略可能不奏效，或在企业销售中遭遇“复杂性与风险”。或者他们可能提供糟糕的客户支持。或者新产品可能失败。或者可能出现技术故障，包括云服务等其他环节的故障。或者他们可能无法完成收购与投资，或无法将其整合，或监管机构可能不批准这些收购。他们可能无法与其他软件集成，或被应用商店下架。

full.sec: You Are Buying Stock In a Company
full.secZh: 你正在买入一家公司的股票

paras.en: On Page 114 they lay out the reasons why, if you buy common stock of a company newly trading on the stock exchange, it might go down instead of up.
paras.zh: 在第 114 页，他们列出了理由，说明为什么如果你买入一家刚在证券交易所上市交易公司的普通股，它可能不涨反跌。

paras.en: Did you know there might be rumors, or market speculation, or more buyers than sellers, or particular sellers, or changes in performance, or volatility, or changes in trading volume, or changing financial projections, or that just generally stocks sometimes go down, including other correlated stocks? That competitors might announce new products, or the public might not like press releases, or there might be public research published that is unfavorable or inaccurate or both? That the float size might change, or new shares might be issued, or new laws passed, or economic conditions might change, or they might be sued, or there might be actual or anticipated changes or fluctuations in the result of Anthropic's operations?
paras.zh: 你是否知道，可能存在谣言、市场投机、买方多于卖方、特定卖方、业绩变化、波动性、交易量变化、财务预测变化，或者一般而言股票有时会下跌，包括其他相关股票？竞争对手可能发布新产品，或者公众可能不喜欢新闻稿，或者可能发表不利或不准确或两者兼有的公开研究？流通股规模可能变化，或者可能发行新股，或者通过新法律，或者经济状况可能变化，或者他们可能被起诉，或者 Anthropic 的运营结果可能存在实际或预期的变化或波动？

paras.en: Not for the foreseeable future. You have been warned.
paras.zh: 在可预见的未来不会。特此警告。

paras.en: I think this is a mistake. I like the Nvidia strategy of issuing a $0.01 dividend, which allows you to be included in various indexes.
paras.zh: 我认为这是一个错误。我喜欢 Nvidia 的策略，即发行 0.01 美元的股息，这能让你被纳入各种指数。

paras.en: We also learn the stock limits, in case there is ever a fun related Matt Levine column: 300 billion Class A shares, 100 billion Class N shares, 30 billion Class E shares, 30 billion shares of preferred stock and the single Class F and single Class T shares.
paras.zh: 我们还了解到股票上限，以防将来有一篇有趣的 Matt Levine 相关专栏：3000 亿股 A 类股、1000 亿股 N 类股、300 亿股 E 类股、300 亿股优先股，以及单一 F 类股和单一 T 类股。

paras.en: There might be a war. Terrorism. Natural disaster. Health crisis. Political crisis.
paras.zh: 可能会有战争。恐怖主义。自然灾害。健康危机。政治危机。

paras.en: The more I read the risks section, the more I understand what it is doing. This is my first S-1, and this is how you play the game of 'list everything that could possibly go wrong, one way or another.'
paras.zh: 我越读风险部分，就越明白它在做什么。这是我的第一份 S-1，而这就是玩“以某种方式列出所有可能出错的事情”这个游戏的方式。

paras.en: I could go on. I won't. Around page 90 I started barely skimming the titles. Tax laws could change. ESG disputes could arise. Yeah, yeah. Why are we doing this?
paras.zh: 我可以继续列下去。但我不会。大约到第 90 页时，我开始几乎只扫一眼标题。税法可能会变。ESG 争议可能会出现。是啊，是啊。我们为什么要做这个？

paras.en: It's a fun game in some senses, but you would not want to read the results. A Pangram spot check says these sections are a mix of AI and not-AI. If anything I would have used AI more.
paras.zh: 从某种意义上说，这是个有趣的游戏，但你不会想读结果。Pangram 抽查显示，这些部分是 AI 和非 AI 的混合。要说的话，我本来会用更多 AI。

paras.en: This is the perfect case for AI writing. It is text no one needs to write, and text no one needs to read. It is all pro forma, a thing that has to exist so that if anyone asks 'does this exist?' the answer comes back yes. It is a gotcha list of gotchas, and we gotcha.
paras.zh: 这是 AI 写作的完美案例。这是没人需要写的文本，也是没人需要读的文本。它全是形式性的，是一种必须存在的东西，这样如果有人问‘这个存在吗？’，答案就会是肯定的。它是一份陷阱清单的陷阱清单，而我们上当了。

paras.en: I have been told that, while that might be its purpose, the gotchas are extremely expensive if someone is got, and that lines are gone over one at a time by committees charging $10k an hour that will be some of the last human cognitive jobs on the planet. I get where that rent seeking comes from, and for Anthropic I guess you just pay the bandits, but I don't see why it changes anything, especially since there is no real penalty that I can see for warning too much about too many things.
paras.zh: 有人告诉我，尽管那可能是其目的，但一旦有人被“坑”到，代价极其高昂；而且这些界线是由收费每小时 1 万美元的委员会逐条审议的，而这些委员会的工作将是地球上最后一批人类认知类工作。我明白这种寻租行为从何而来，对 Anthropic 来说，我猜你只能向这些“劫匪”付钱，但我不明白这为什么会改变什么，尤其是因为我看不出对过多事情发出过多警告会有什么真正的惩罚。

items.en: The stock market operates on 'normal' financial models, so we get a normal financial model. Anthropic invests in compute, uses compute, sells compute, and operates.
items.zh: 股票市场基于“正常”的财务模型运行，因此我们得到一个正常的财务模型。Anthropic 投资于算力、使用算力、销售算力并运营。

items.en: In some senses, I suppose this is a model? It is a very high-level model, I suppose.
items.zh: 在某些意义上，我想这是一个模型？我想，这是一个非常高层级的模型。

items.en: **Our Financial Model**
items.zh: **我们的财务模型**

items.en: Our financial model is built on four primary drivers that define the trajectory of our results:
items.zh: 我们的财务模型建立在四个主要驱动因素之上，这些因素定义了我们的业绩轨迹：

items.en: *   _**Adoption of Claude.**_ The advancing intelligence and capabilities of each successive version of a Claude model drive the diffusion of Claude across the global economy. As new customers adopt Claude and existing customers expand their usage into new workflows, our revenue grows.
items.zh: *   _**Claude 的采用。**_ 每个 successive 版本的 Claude 模型不断进步的智能和能力推动了 Claude 在全球经济中的扩散。随着新客户采用 Claude 以及现有客户将其使用扩展到新的工作流程，我们的收入增长。

items.en: *   _**Compute Efficiency.**_ We are focused on increasing the intelligence produced and revenue generated per dollar of compute invested and have delivered significant efficiency improvements.
items.zh: *   _**算力效率。**_ 我们专注于提高每美元算力投入所产出的智能和所创造的收入，并已实现显著的效率提升。

items.en: *   _**Operating Efficiency.**_ Our high talent density, efficient go-to-market, and how extensively our teams leverage Claude in their work help to drive improved operating margin, Adjusted Operating Margin, and revenue per employee.
items.zh: *   _**运营效率。**_ 我们高密度的人才、高效的上市策略，以及团队在工作中广泛使用 Claude，有助于提升运营利润率、调整后运营利润率以及人均收入。

items.en: *   _**Compute Investments.**_ Investing in compute is critical to support our long-term growth, and we intend to continue making substantial investments in compute.
items.zh: *   _**算力投资。**_ 投资算力对于支撑我们的长期增长至关重要，我们打算继续在算力上进行大规模投资。

items.en: The drivers of our financial model materialize on different timelines.
items.zh: 我们财务模型的各项驱动因素会在不同的时间线上逐步显现。

items.en: Claude is sold through all three major cloud platforms (AWS, GCP and Azure) and through various other methods. Growth is what we call ‘gangbusters.’
items.zh: Claude 通过全部三大云平台（AWS、GCP 和 Azure）以及多种其他渠道销售。增长可谓‘异常迅猛’。

items.en: Our customers with $100k or more of revenue on a TTM basis included every company in the Fortune 10, over 50% of the Fortune 500, and over 30% of the Global 2000.
items.zh: 我们以 TTM 口径计算收入达到 10 万美元及以上的客户，覆盖了《财富》10 强中的每一家公司、《财富》500 强中超过 50% 的公司，以及全球 2000 强中超过 30% 的公司。

items.en: Within the Fortune 500, these customers included the 10 largest software and IT services companies, the 10 largest internet companies, nine of the 10 largest pharmaceutical companies, the 10 largest banks, nine of the 10 largest semiconductor companies, and eight of the 10 largest healthcare companies.
items.zh: 在《财富》500 强中，这些客户包括 10 家最大的软件与 IT 服务公司、10 家最大的互联网公司、10 家最大制药公司中的 9 家、10 家最大的银行、10 家最大半导体公司中的 9 家，以及 10 家最大医疗健康公司中的 8 家。

items.en: On top of that, existing customers have Net Revenue Retention of ~900%. Which is good, because the above could be called 'market saturation.'
items.zh: 除此之外，现有客户的净收入留存率（Net Revenue Retention）约为 900%。这是好事，因为上述情况本可以被称为“市场饱和”。

items.en: Next up is compute efficiency, which then breaks down into training efficiency (going up), inference efficiency (going up) and multi-chip compute approach.
items.zh: 接下来是算力效率，它又可细分为训练效率（正在提升）、推理效率（正在提升）以及多芯片算力方案。

items.en: Compute is getting increasingly efficiently turned into revenue.
items.zh: 算力正越来越高效地转化为收入。

items.capEn: Operating efficiency is up. More is being operated by less people per operation.
items.capZh: 运营效率在提升。每次运营由更少的人操作更多的事务。

items.en: Anthropic then sells Claude inference, including via subscriptions.
items.zh: 随后，Anthropic 出售 Claude 的推理服务，包括通过订阅方式提供。

items.en: They then work with customers as they integrate Claude into workflows and use more Claude for more of the things over time.
items.zh: 接着，他们与客户合作，帮助客户将 Claude 集成到工作流中，并随着时间推移在更多事务上使用更多 Claude。

items.en: This 'model' does not allow you to predict much, other than 'wow, it looks like numbers are going up and getting better, perhaps they will make a lot of money.'
items.zh: 这个“模型”并不能让你预测太多，除了“哇，看起来数字在上升、在变好，也许他们会赚很多钱”。

items.en: You can tell the model is not that useful since the 'key factors affecting our performance' then get repeated from earlier without being directly in the model.
items.zh: 你可以看出这个模型并没有那么有用，因为“影响我们业绩的关键因素”随后只是从前面重复了一遍，而并未直接纳入模型之中。

items.en: They also repeat a bunch of the financial number statements in adjusted form.
items.zh: 他们还以调整后的形式重复了若干财务数字陈述。

items.en: Later, when evaluating the fair value of the common stock pre-IPO, the board of directors 'exercised reasonable judgment and considered numerous objective and subjective factors,' including:
items.zh: 后来，在评估 IPO 前普通股的公允价值时，董事会“行使了合理判断，并考虑了众多客观和主观因素”，包括：

items.en: 3. Whether there will be more buyers than sellers, or more sellers than buyers.
items.zh: 3. 买方是否会多于卖方，或卖方是否会多于买方。

items.en: Oh, sorry, I am informed that instead they claim they looked at other things, but hey.
items.zh: 哦，抱歉，我被告知他们实际上声称考察了其他方面，但嘿。

full.sec: The Business of Intelligence and Maybe Killing Everyone
full.secZh: 智能的商业，以及可能杀死所有人

items.en: There is a lot of repetition in an S-1. The ‘business’ section goes over a lot of the same facts from earlier, that I’ve already gone over.
items.zh: S-1 文件中有很多重复内容。“业务”部分会再次讨论前面已经出现过的许多相同事实，而我已经在前面讨论过了。

items.en: This is where they get gathered together, and get to emphasize ‘hey did you know Claude is increasingly able to do all the digital things and also interface with the physical things, and it’s going to keep improving and follow the scaling laws?’
items.zh: 这里是将它们汇总在一起的地方，并借此强调：“嘿，你知道 Claude 越来越能够完成所有数字任务，还能与物理世界交互，并且它会持续进步并遵循缩放定律吗？”

items.capEn: If you’re reading this, you already know Claude is going to do all the things, and which products will be used to do that, so this is about how that is being presented to investors. There is no way to properly convey what Claude can do in an S-1, or the true vision of what is coming, especially without worrying about securities fraud if things do not work out so well.
items.capZh: 如果你正在读这篇文章，你已然知道 Claude 将完成所有事情，也知道哪些产品会被用来实现这些，所以这里讨论的是如何向投资者呈现这一点。在 S-1 文件中，无法恰当地传达 Claude 能做什么，或者即将到来的真正愿景，尤其是如果事情进展不顺利，还要担心证券欺诈。

items.en: But yeah, It’s Coming. They say what they can for those with eyes to see.
items.zh: 但是，是的，它正在到来。他们对那些有眼能看的人说了他们能说的话。

items.en: **All digital work is ultimately an expression of code**, and Claude’s mastery of it powers Virtual Collaborators capable of handling complex work far beyond software development.
items.zh: **所有数字工作最终都是代码的一种表达**，而 Claude 对代码的精通驱动了虚拟协作者，能够处理远超软件开发的复杂工作。

items.en: … We are building towards a world where Claude can be given open-ended tasks lasting hours, days, or weeks, and then execute them autonomously with the judgment and initiative of a brilliant colleague.
items.zh: ……我们正在迈向这样一个世界：Claude 可以被赋予持续数小时、数天或数周的无限制任务，然后以一位才华横溢的同事般的判断力和主动性自主执行这些任务。

items.en: … A core driver of Claude’s diffusion is its intelligence.
items.zh: ……Claude 扩散的一个核心驱动力是其智能。

items.en: … Each new primitive and application we release expands the range of workflows they can run on Claude.
items.zh: ……我们发布的每一个新原语和应用都扩展了它们可以在 Claude 上运行的工作流范围。

items.en: You do have to extrapolate a bit, or you miss most of what is going to be happening.
items.zh: 你确实需要做一些外推，否则你会错过即将发生的大部分事情。

items.en: Otherwise, how many times can you say you will do the various good things? A lot.
items.zh: 否则，你能说多少次你会做各种好事？很多次。

items.en: They spell out what all their current products are: Claude [Code / Cowork / .ai / Security / Tag / Design / Science]. You've got Claude for [Financial Services / Financial Advisors / Healthcare / Life Sciences / Legal / Education / Government]. It's all Claude.
items.zh: 他们明确列出了当前所有产品：Claude [Code / Cowork / .ai / Security / Tag / Design / Science]。还有面向[金融服务 / 财务顾问 / 医疗健康 / 生命科学 / 法律 / 教育 / 政府]的 Claude。全都是 Claude。

items.en: One term that was new to me was Prosumers, which I think stands for 'professional consumers' and means individual Pro or Max subscribers. I'm a prosumer.
items.zh: 有一个我此前没听过的词是 Prosumers，我认为它代表“专业消费者”（professional consumers），指个人版 Pro 或 Max 订阅用户。我就是一名 prosumer。

items.en: They show off and highlight successful partnerships with Accenture, AIG (oh no, is this alphabetical? It looks like it is alphabetical), Bristol Myers Squibb, DoorDash, International Rescue Committee, Jane Street, Legora, Lilly, Mercado Libre, Mozilla, PayPal, Rakuten, Salesforce, SAP, Shopify, Travelers, UST, Verizon, Walmart, and featuring Shy Bird and KBF.
items.zh: 他们展示并强调了与以下公司的成功合作：Accenture、AIG（哦不，这是按字母顺序排的吗？看起来确实是按字母顺序）、Bristol Myers Squibb、DoorDash、International Rescue Committee、Jane Street、Legora、Lilly、Mercado Libre、Mozilla、PayPal、Rakuten、Salesforce、SAP、Shopify、Travelers、UST、Verizon、Walmart，并特别提及 Shy Bird 和 KBF。

items.en: Different companies offer different stats and use cases. The gains look large for those who do a lot of coding. Coding outputs seem credibly to be +100% or more. For others it is modest, such as PayPal's 45 minutes saved per sales team member per week. Then again, is ~2% time saved from a custom-built plugin not much, or is it a lot? What about the 25 hours per month saved per consultant at SAP, or ~14%? Over the next year I expect that answer to change.
items.zh: 不同公司给出的数据和用例各不相同。对于大量编写代码的用户，收益看起来很大。代码产出可信地达到 +100% 或更高。对其他用户而言则较为有限，例如 PayPal 每位销售团队成员每周节省 45 分钟。话说回来，一个定制插件节省约 2% 的时间，算少还是算多？SAP 每位顾问每月节省 25 小时，约 14%，又该怎么看？我预计在未来一年内，这个答案会发生变化。

full.sec: Don’t Give a Damn About My Regulation
full.secZh: 别对我的监管毫不在意

paras.en: Anthropic reiterates its position, and paints itself as pro-regulation.
paras.zh: Anthropic 重申其立场，并将自己描绘成支持监管的一方。

paras.en: We believe that the responsible development of AI requires thoughtful governance, and we actively support efforts by governments and regulatory bodies to establish frameworks that promote safe, beneficial AI. We were founded on the premise that AI systems must be developed with safety and societal benefit as central priorities, and we believe that well-designed regulation can reinforce those values across the industry.
paras.zh: 我们认为，负责任的 AI 发展需要深思熟虑的治理，我们积极支持政府和监管机构建立促进安全、有益 AI 的框架的努力。我们成立的前提是，AI 系统的开发必须以安全和社会效益为核心优先事项，我们相信精心设计的监管可以在整个行业强化这些价值观。

paras.en: Because AI development at the frontier is a relatively nascent and rapidly evolving field, the laws, regulations, and standards in place today were not necessarily designed with these technologies in mind. We have proactively engaged with legislators, regulators, and other stakeholders in the United States and internationally to promote the development of regulatory frameworks that we believe are good for society, our customers, and the long-term health of the economy, and we intend to continue doing so.
paras.zh: 由于前沿 AI 开发是一个相对新生且快速发展的领域，当前的法律、法规和标准未必是针对这些技术设计的。我们主动与美国及国际的立法者、监管者和其他利益相关者接触，以推动制定我们认为对社会、客户和经济长期健康有益的监管框架，并打算继续这样做。

paras.en: For example, we entered into an agreement with the CAISSI whereby we committed to provide access to our models for testing and evaluation before and after their public release, agreed to provide model access to the U.K. AI Security Institute for pre-deployment testing consistent with our agreement with the CAISSI, and publicly endorsed California’s Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act (SB 53).
paras.zh: 例如，我们与 CAISSI 达成协议，承诺在模型公开发布前后提供模型访问以进行测试和评估，同意根据与 CAISSI 的协议向英国 AI 安全研究所提供模型访问以进行部署前测试，并公开支持加利福尼亚州的《前沿人工智能透明度法案》（SB 53）。

paras.en: See **recent****other****posts** on Anthropic for my response to that. Anthropic is in some ways performing better than other labs, and they do prioritize the provisions they feel are most important, even when they are not the obvious ones. But I do not feel their proposals are meeting the moment, and this is not a new issue.
paras.zh: 关于我的回应，请参阅 Anthropic 的**近期其他文章**。Anthropic 在某些方面表现优于其他实验室，他们确实优先考虑他们认为最重要的条款，即使这些条款不是显而易见的。但我认为他们的提案未能应对当下的挑战，而且这不是一个新问题。

paras.en: This is an S-1, so the actual question here is the impact on Anthropic's bottom line. They don't have that much to say about that, other than laying out some basic past events.
paras.zh: 这是一份 S-1 文件，因此这里真正的问题在于对 Anthropic 利润的影响。除了列举一些基本的过往事件外，他们对此并没有太多说明。

paras.en: Ultimately, the bottom line is the bottom line. The S-1 is all about what investors care about, and what will guard against being sued for securities fraud or otherwise getting the financial types Big Mad at Anthropic. Other audiences are secondary.
paras.zh: 归根结底，底线就是底线。S-1 文件的核心在于投资者关心什么，以及什么能防止公司因证券欺诈被起诉，或避免让金融界人士对 Anthropic 大为光火。其他受众都是次要的。

paras.en: Anthropic remains a frustrating company. Now we know a lot more about it.
paras.zh: Anthropic 仍然是一家令人沮丧的公司。现在我们对它有了更多了解。
